Incisions made parallel to Langer's lines heal better and give narrower scars; those that cross them tend to gape and form hypertrophic scars or keloids. (On the face, follow the relaxed skin tension lines; across joints, avoid straight lines that cross flexor creases.)

qs.q: A patient presents with a severe keloid scar on the anterior chest wall causing restriction and cosmetic concern. Which of the following is a recognized intervention used in the management of keloids?
o: Primary closure performed under high tension
qs.e: Intralesional corticosteroid (triamcinolone) injections, bleomycin, 5-fluorouracil, and cryotherapy are standard management options for keloids. High tension encourages scar formation rather than treating it.
